title: Visual craftsmanship and interaction quality
definition: Visual and interaction details are deliberate and consistent: type scale, spacing, alignment, colour roles, states, motion and response time are specified, implemented and checked rather than left to defaults.
intended_outcome: The interface looks and responds as if made with care: no broken states, layout shift, jank or inconsistent affordances.
implementation_guidance: Define tokens (type, spacing, colour roles, radii, motion durations) in one source file. Components consume tokens; raw values in component CSS are findings.
Every interactive element has default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading and error appearances, and a test or screenshot covers them.
Motion has a purpose (state change, orientation), respects prefers-reduced-motion and never delays a task.
Check the narrowest supported width and a wide width. No horizontal page scroll.
Run the design tooling's anti-pattern scan on rendered pages in the Claude session and record the findings. The product's own DESIGN.md prohibitions are the checklist.

automated: Token usage check: raw colour and spacing literals outside the token file.
Rendered-page checks: no horizontal overflow at the narrowest width; focus visible.
expert_review: Design critique against the product DESIGN.md prohibitions.
observed_behaviour: Interaction timing from real sessions where telemetry exists.

limitations: Craft is partly aesthetic judgement. Automated checks catch defects, not quality.
Anti-pattern scanners encode their authors' taste.

evidence.summary: The owner directs that products have a distinctive, sophisticated and trustworthy experience.
Specified and tested states prevent the broken-state defects that undermine trust.
evidence.rationale: Reasoned from common defect types; not measured on Dot products.
